text:
Alex: Heads-up — saw a regression on the 8xA100_PP4_TP2 job when rematerialization is enabled. tail of request latency distribution spiked (p95->p99).
Maria: Hmm, when did this start? commit/rollout?
Alex: Rolled a scheduler change and a kernel routing tweak yesterday morning (canary). Noticed after enabling remat for the new 30k-seqlen path.
Rui: Can you paste the perf traces? short snippets are fine.
Alex: Pasting the critical slice from `nsys` + our perf counters:
```
# timeline excerpt (condensed)
0.00s compute(op L0): 20ms
0.02s allreduce(size=128MB) queued: 120ms wait
0.14s compute(op L1): 10ms
0.15s recompute(stage 2): 35ms  # remat triggered extra compute on PP ranks
0.20s allreduce queued: 180ms  <-- observed ramp
0.38s nvtx: kernel_switch(triton_gemm_fp16) latency +9ms
```
Alex: The pattern: remat causes extra compute on pipeline stages that used to be idle during forward; this pushes more NCCL work simultaneously and we see all-reduce queueing.
Casey: Does KV cache traffic affect this? I remember we had prefix-cache flushes landing on rank0 and stalling comms.
Alex: Yes — interestingly, the liveliness of KV requests increased on the same ranks that do more recompute because of our shard placement. When a large prefix hits, we also do a small reduce for logits scattering and that collides with the all-reduces.
Maria: Do we have per-rank overlap metrics? like compute-utilization vs nccl-wait?
Alex: Yup — attaching summaries (text):
```
rank0: compute_util=78%, nccl_wait=28ms/s, remat_extra=12%
rank1: compute_util=82%, nccl_wait=45ms/s, remat_extra=15%
rank2..3: compute_util=55%, nccl_wait=8ms/s, remat_extra=2%
```
Rui: That imbalance looks like TP+PP boundary ranks taking the hit. If remat duplicates compute on boundary layers we amplify all-reduce fan-in.
Casey: Any kernel-level surprises? e.g., suboptimal GEMM path selected during remat batches?
Alex: Good catch — profiler shows fallback to slower matmul kernel for short sequence segments during remat. Kernel selector picks a different tiling because batch shapes are more fragmented post-remat. That adds a few ms per kernel and widens windows where multiple NCCL ops can pile up.
Maria: Could batching heuristics help? coalesce remat recompute work or enforce staggering?
Rui: Two mitigation ideas: 1) stagger remat across microbatches so all-reduces for recompute don't align; 2) prefer deterministic kernel routing that favors lower variance for those boundaries.
Alex: Tried a quick software staggering hack: delay recompute kick-off on odd PP stages by 2ms. Result: all-reduce queue time dropped ~40% on the worst rank and tail latency improved. No functional change.
Casey: Any risks with staggering? affects p99 under tiny budgets?
Alex: Main tradeoff is small extra latency per request on average (1–2ms) vs big p99 wins. But it interacts with batching: if you stagger and batcher coalesces, you might re-align them again. Need careful ordering between batcher and remat scheduler.
Maria: What about KV cache placement? can we rebalance KV traffic away from remat-heavy ranks?
Alex: We can try sharding KV differently — move hot prefixes to ranks with lower remat load. That helped in a toy run. Also considered offloading KV maintenance to a separate thread so it doesn't block NCCL streams.
Rui: Also check NCCL stream priorities and CUDA graphs — we might be serializing operations inadvertently. Using async-progress+dedicated CUDA stream for NCCL reduced queuing in one test.
InfraBot: deploy canary completed: scheduler-change v2 on cluster-pp-4 at 2026-02-17T09:42Z
Casey: Good note. Next steps?
Alex: Plan: 1) add a remat staggering scheduler in runtime (opt-in flag) 2) adjust kernel selector to prefer low-jitter kernels near PP/TP boundaries 3) experiment with KV shard rebalancing 4) NCCL stream/priority tweak + rerun perf sweep.
Maria: Can you open a small PR with the flag and a perf test that reproduces the queueing? put the nsys snippet and ranks summary in the description.
Alex: Will do. I'll also attach a short flamegraph and a diff that shows where remat scheduling triggers.
Rui: If you need infra for larger sweeps I can reserve a 8xA100 pool tomorrow.
Alex: Thanks — will ping once PR is up. For tracker: linking to internal perf task INF-1357 in the PR.
Casey: :thumbsup: nice debugging thread.
Alex: TL;DR — rematerialization increases compute overlap at PP/TP boundaries, causing NCCL all-reduce queueing amplified by kernel selection and KV cache hotspots. Early mitigations (staggering + kernel routing) effective. Need broader perf sweep and a stable runtime flag.
